reference.title: Display and positioning
reference.shortdesc: The display property determines the kind of box an element generates. Positioning properties describe how a box is placed relative to its normal position or containing block.

section.title: Display properties

row.entry: Name
Description
Values
Default
Specification
Selects whether an element generates a box and describes its outer and inner display types.

none, contents, or combinations of outer types (block, inline, run-in), inner types (flow, flow-root, table, flex, grid, ruby), and list-item; also internal table and ruby types, legacy combinations such as inline-block, inline-flex, and inline-grid, plus math, grid-lanes, and inline-grid-lanes
Controls whether a box is visible while preserving its place in layout.
visible, hidden, force-hidden, or collapse
Changes the order of flex and grid items for layout and painting.
An integer
Chooses the reading order of children in a block, flex, or grid container.
normal, source-order, flex-visual, flex-flow, grid-rows, grid-columns, or grid-order
Assigns an integer ordering value to a direct child of a reading-flow container.
An integer

section.p: An integer is a whole number without a fractional part. Negative values, zero, and positive values are allowed for order; CSS Display defines how ordering is applied.

Description
Values
Default
Specification
Chooses the positioning scheme for an element.
static, relative, absolute, sticky, fixed, or running()
CSS Position 3 §2; CSS GCPM 3 §1.2.1
top, right, bottom, left
Set an inset from the corresponding side of the containing block for a positioned element.
auto, a length or percentage, anchor(), or anchor-size()
Sets the four physical insets.
One to four values accepted by top, right, bottom, and left
inset-block, inset-inline
Set the start and end insets along the block or inline axis.
One or two values accepted by the corresponding logical inset properties
inset-block-start, inset-block-end, inset-inline-start, inset-inline-end
Set one inset on the block or inline axis.
auto, a length or percentage, anchor(), or anchor-size()
Sets a positioned box’s stack level.
auto or an integer
Names properties that are expected to change. A box that names a property gets the containing block and the stacking context that some value of that property would give it; nothing else changes.
auto, or a list of property names, scroll-position, and contents

ul.li: A length is a size with a unit, such as 12pt or 1em. A percentage is relative to the containing block, as defined for the relevant inset.

anchor() gives the place of an edge of an anchor, an element named with anchor-name: anchor(an optional anchor name, an edge, and an optional fallback after a comma). The edge is top, right, bottom or left in an inset of the same axis, start, end, self-start, self-end, inside, outside, center or a percentage. Without a name it uses the default anchor that position-anchor gives. When the anchor is missing, the inset takes the fallback, or auto without one. It resolves only on a box with position: absolute or position: fixed; on other boxes it takes its fallback, and a declaration without one has no effect. See CSS Anchor Positioning 1 §3.2.

anchor-size() gives the size of an anchor in a size, an inset or a margin: anchor-size(an optional anchor name, an optional width, height, block, inline, self-block or self-inline, and an optional fallback after a comma). Without a keyword it gives the size along the axis of the property. Like anchor(), it resolves only on an absolutely positioned or fixed box. See CSS Anchor Positioning 1 §5.1.

A box with position: fixed is placed against the page area, and every page shows it, blank pages included. Its insets are measured from the edges of the page area. When you give no inset on an axis, the box keeps on every page the place its element has on the page where it falls in the text, or, inside a running element, the place where the running element was. A link to the element goes to the first page, and a footnote in the box is placed once, at the foot of the first page. When an ancestor has a transform, contain: layout or contain: paint, or names one of those properties in will-change, the box is placed against that ancestor instead, and it is drawn once, with the ancestor. A fixed box is a stacking context even when its z-index is auto, and so is a box with layout or paint containment. The overflow clipping of the boxes around a fixed box does not cut it. See CSS Position 3 §3.1.

A box with position: absolute and no positioned ancestor is placed against the page area of the page where it falls in the text, whatever part of that page the text fills, or against the footnote area inside a footnote. A positioned inline element is the containing block of the positioned boxes inside it, with a rectangle that covers all its lines. See CSS Position 3 §3.5.3.

A containing block that breaks across pages places its positioned boxes against the whole block, its parts joined, and each box is drawn on the page where its place falls. A positioned box that reaches past the end of a page goes on at the top of the next page. See CSS Fragmentation 4 §5.5.
A box with position: sticky stays where the text puts it, since a page does not scroll. It is a containing block and a stacking context, as a relative box is.
running() names an element to move into a page margin box. See CSS GCPM 3.
An integer is a whole number without a fractional part. Negative values, zero, and positive values are allowed for z-index.

row.entry: Makes the element an anchor that positioned boxes can find by name. An element or a ::before or ::after pseudo-element can be an anchor. When several elements have a name, a box uses the nearest of its ancestors that has it, or else the last one in the document.
none, or one or more names that start with two hyphens, such as --figure, separated by commas
Keeps the anchor names it lists inside the element: a positioned box inside the element finds only the anchors inside it with those names, and a box outside finds none of them.
none, all, or one or more anchor names separated by commas

Gives a positioned box its default anchor, which position-area, anchor-center and the anchor functions without a name use. auto uses the element of a ::before or ::after pseudo-element, and an element has none. normal is auto when position-area is set and none otherwise. match-parent uses the default anchor of the parent.
normal, none, auto, an anchor name, or match-parent

Places a positioned box in cells of the three by three grid that its default anchor makes in its containing block. The area becomes the containing block, and the auto insets and auto margins are zero. With normal alignment the box stands against the anchor. Without a default anchor it has no effect. A single keyword acts as if the other were span-all, or as if it were repeated when it fits both axes.

none, or one or two keywords for a row and a column: a cell, such as top, center, right, block-start, inline-end, self-block-end, x-start or y-end, or a cell and the middle one, such as span-left or span-block-end, or span-all

Lists other places to try when the box sticks out of its containing block. The first place in which the box fits is used, and the box keeps its own place when none fits. A tactic flips the insets, margins, alignment and area of the box to the other side of its anchor, and flip-start swaps its axes and sizes.

none, or entries separated by commas: a position-area value, or the name of an @position-try rule, tactics, or both; a name that no rule has is skipped. The tactics are flip-block, flip-inline, flip-start, flip-x and flip-y
Tries first the places that leave the box the most room along an axis. normal keeps the order of the list.
normal, most-width, most-height, most-block-size or most-inline-size
Sets position-try-order and position-try-fallbacks.
An optional value of position-try-order, then a value of position-try-fallbacks

Names a place for position-try-fallbacks. Its declarations replace those of the box while the place is tried. It accepts the insets, the margins, the sizes, justify-self, align-self, position-anchor and position-area; other declarations, and declarations with !important, are ignored.
@position-try --name { declarations }
None

Hides a positioned box. anchors-visible hides it when its default anchor is invisible or clipped away entirely by an overflow, a clip-path or contain: paint between the anchor and the containing block. anchors-valid hides it when an anchor it needs is missing. no-overflow hides it when it sticks out of its containing block. always never hides it.
always, or one or more of anchors-valid, anchors-visible and no-overflow

Places a block box, or an absolutely positioned box, along the inline axis of its containing block. A block box with a value other than normal or stretch and no width is as wide as its content. Auto margins come first. Floats and anonymous blocks ignore it. auto takes the justify-items of the parent, except for an absolutely positioned box placed by its insets, where it is normal. anchor-center centers a positioned box on its default anchor, and is center elsewhere.
auto, normal, stretch, baseline, first baseline, last baseline, anchor-center, or center, start, end, self-start, self-end, flex-start, flex-end, left or right, with safe or unsafe before it
CSS Box Alignment 3 §6.1; CSS Anchor Positioning 1 §4.2

Places an absolutely positioned box along the block axis of its containing block. auto takes the align-items of the parent where the box stands at its place in the text, and is normal otherwise. It has no effect on block boxes.
The values of justify-self except left and right
Sets align-self and justify-self. With one value both take it.
A value of align-self, then an optional value of justify-self
The value that justify-self: auto takes in the children of the element. legacy with left, right or center passes that keyword on to the descendants whose own value is legacy.
normal, stretch, a baseline value, a position of justify-self with an optional safe or unsafe, legacy, or legacy with left, right or center
The value that align-self: auto takes in the children of the element.
normal, stretch, a baseline value, or a position of align-self with an optional safe or unsafe
Sets align-items and justify-items. With one value both take it.
A value of align-items, then an optional value of justify-items
